name: context-menu
title: Context Menu
summary: The menu a right-click opens on a row, a file or a canvas.
description: The menu a right-click opens on a row, a file or a canvas. The Menu, opened on an area instead of a button: a right-click (or a long press on a touch screen, or the context-menu key) opens it at the pointer, with the same rows, options, groups and sub-menus. The area is yours (a row, a card, a canvas); the popup, the gliding highlight and the keyboard are the Menu's. Behaviour from the Zag menu machine through Ark UI.

anatomy.description: The area (Ark's context trigger, as a div around your content). A right-click inside it opens the Menu at the pointer instead of the browser's menu; a long press does on touch. It takes no look of its own. On a coarse pointer it is not text-selectable and shows no callout, so the long press reaches the menu. The popup is the Menu's (menu-positioner, menu-content, menu-highlight, menu-item …).

items.description: Entries in order, exactly as the Menu takes them.

disabled.description: The area keeps the browser's own context menu.

label.description: The area's accessible name (aria-label). The area is focusable: Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the menu from it.

open.description: Controlled: open with onOpenChange. It opens at the last pointer position, so it needs one: before any right-click (or long press, or Shift+F10) on the area, open=true is refused. The menu stays closed, moves no focus, and onOpenChange(false) puts the host's state right. Once a right-click has given a position, open=true opens the menu there.

keyboard: Tab reaches the area itself (tabIndex 0, role group, aria-keyshortcuts Shift+F10, the global focus ring); Shift+F10 or the context-menu key with focus on or inside it opens the menu (the browser's contextmenu event)
Inside, the Menu's keys: ArrowDown / ArrowUp, Home / End, type-ahead, Enter / Space, sub-menus with ArrowRight / ArrowLeft
Escape closes; focus returns to the area, or to the element inside it that had focus
notes: A context menu is a shortcut: everything in it must also be reachable another way (a visible Menu button, a toolbar), since a right-click is not discoverable.

It never opens without a pointer position: mounted with open=true, or told to open before any right-click on the area, it stays closed, moves no focus and reports closed through openChange. To open a menu from a button or at mount, use the Menu.
The area is focusable by itself; give it a name with `label` (its aria-label) when its text does not say what it is.

motion: the Menu's popup: opacity + scale from motion.popup-scale out of the pointer position, duration.popup, easing.out-strong; closes at duration.fast; instant from the keyboard
